name: Ashford & Reyes BCI-Responsive Chromatic Tuxedo
description:
Ashford & Reyes is a two-person atelier operating out of a Tier 4 studio in the upper commercial district, producing approximately forty garments per year. Their chromatic tuxedo is constructed from a base of real-wool barathea — sourced at considerable expense from a vertical farm operation in the northern corridor — overlaid with a micro-woven BCI-responsive chromatic layer that reads ambient emotional and physiological data from the wearer's neural interface and shifts the fabric's surface sheen accordingly. At rest, the tuxedo reads as flat black. Under stress, the lapels develop a deep blue iridescence. During elevated social engagement, a warm bronze tone bleeds through the chest. The wearer cannot fully control it; they can only learn to work with it.

The construction is entirely by hand, requiring twelve to eighteen fittings. Augment accommodations are custom — each tuxedo is built around the specific chrome, geneware, or modification profile of its wearer, with no generic openings but precise ones. A client with functional geneware wings receives back panels with integrated support architecture. A client with full-arm chrome receives sleeve construction that treats the augment as part of the garment's structure. The price is per consultation quote, but Φ3,200 is the published floor.
cultural_context: The chromatic tuxedo's BCI-responsiveness makes it simultaneously intimate and exposed — the garment broadcasts physiological states that social convention normally conceals. In Tier 4-5 circles, wearing one is a calculated vulnerability: a signal that you are confident enough to let the room see your reactions. Some clients disable the chromatic layer entirely after the first event, having underestimated what they were agreeing to display.
story_hooks: A Vantablack intelligence analyst attends a Tier 5 event in this tuxedo, unaware that the BCI-responsive layer is broadcasting data that a trained observer can read as a stress response map — effectively narrating their reactions to everything in the room.
Ashford or Reyes recognizes a client's emotional profile in the chromatic shifts and realizes the person wearing their tuxedo is not the person they fitted it for.
The real-wool barathea is traced to a vertical farm operation that is quietly under Arcturus quarantine — and the garment may carry something the wearer doesn't know about.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sharply tailored formal jacket and trousers silhouette that reads as elegant minimalism at first glance—but the fabric surface subtly shifts with the wearer's emotional state. At rest, it presents as deep matte black with an almost liquid surface tension. The cut is precise, slightly high-waisted, with a modern architectural quality that echoes haute couture rather than traditional black-tie.
physical_description.fit: Bespoke tailored; fits the body like a second skin without restricting movement. Jacket sits at the natural waist with gently suppressed sides. Trousers have a straight leg with minimal break. The fit accounts for the wearer's specific augmentations—no generic cutaways, but seamless integration where chrome or geneware meets fabric.
physical_description.primary_material: Real-wool barathea (expensive, vertically farmed) as base layer, overlaid with proprietary micro-woven BCI-responsive chromatic mesh. The surface is a hybrid construction—structured but responsive.
physical_description.texture: Smooth and fluid to the touch, with a subtle woven microstructure visible under close inspection. The chromatic layer sits atop the barathea like a second skin, creating a barely-perceptible depth. The fabric has a slight grip quality—it doesn't slide off the body.
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep black at rest (matte with liquid undertones). Under stress or heightened emotion, the lapels and chest develop an iridescent blue-to-bronze gradient. During social engagement or elevated heart rate, warm bronze and copper tones bleed through. The shifts are organic, never fully controlled by the wearer.
physical_description.closures: Magnetic snap closure on the jacket front (silent, seamless activation). Trousers feature a friction-fit waistband requiring no visible fastening. All closures are deliberately minimal and premium—nothing that breaks the visual line.
distinctive_features: BCI-responsive chromatic overlay that shifts based on wearer's emotional/physiological state
Completely custom-fitted augmentation accommodations (no generic openings)
Seamless integration with chrome, geneware, or biological modifications
Subtle neural interface connection points, invisible unless you know where to look
Lapels and chest serve as primary chromatic response zones
Barely-visible topstitching in matte black thread
Optional chromatic layer disable switch (rarely used after initial shock)
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 4-5 bespoke luxury—the price floor is Φ3,200, and full consultation quotes easily exceed Φ5,000+. Only attainable for those with serious currency or corp backing.
physical_description.cultural_context: A statement of calculated vulnerability and neural confidence. Wearing this in Tier 4-5 social spaces signals: I am augmented, I am wealthy enough to afford radical transparency, and I am secure enough to let the room read my physiological state in real time. It's simultaneously intimate and exposing—the garment is a confession written in fabric. Some wearers love this; others disable the chromatic layer after one event, realizing they've revealed more than intended.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine. Handmade pieces of this caliber are maintained meticulously. The fabric shows no wear in normal use; it's engineered for longevity. Over time, the wearer develops a relationship with their tuxedo—learning which situations trigger which color responses, eventually treating the chromatic shifts as part of their personal presentation.

image_prompt: A bespoke chromatic tuxedo on an androgynous neo-noir model in a minimalist Tier 4 atelier studio. The model has visible neural interface ports at the temple and subtle chrome augmentation on one forearm. The tuxedo's black fabric is sharp and tailored, but the chest and lapels show a subtle blue-bronze iridescence—mid-emotional response. Moody studio lighting with cold neon accents reflecting off the chromatic surface. The background is a sleek, neutral grey wall with soft depth-of-field bokeh. Shallow depth of field on the jacket's responsive chromatic zones. Hyper-detailed fabric texture visible. Neo-noir haute couture editorial aesthetic. --ar 2:3 --v 6
